Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

next to preposition and adverb

also beside, by (close to), close beside, at someone’s side

classical

Caes. BC 1.16.4: juxtā mūrum castra posuit (Lewis & Short)
Sall. Jug. 65.2: ut sellam juxtā pōneret

1juxtā: u left unmarked (the earlier draft of this record, jūxtā). Lewis & Short marks only the final ā, and the lexicon’s other records and the Latinitas loci write juxtā. De Vaan 318, s.v. juxta, derives it from Proto-Italic *jougVsto-, which would give a long u, but does not discuss the vowel. Left unmarked until it is settled.

juxtā1

adverb, and preposition with the accusative

next to, beside, close by

As an adverb, close by, at someone’s side: sellam juxtā pōnere. As a preposition it is not found before Caesar (Lewis & Short): juxtā focum, by the fire. Its other sense, “equally, just as” (juxtā ac sī), is not this one.

Other words

  • propter + acc. — beside, close to

    preposition with the accusative; also an adverb, close by · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 24: in prātulō propter Platōnis statuam cōnsēdimus; Ter. Ad. 170: hīc propter hunc adsiste

    Rare but classical in this sense (Lewis & Short). Its everyday sense is “because of” (see due to), so keep it for a place plainly meant. For “by” a door or a gate, ad (see at); for “near”, prope.

Examples

  • hīc propter hunc adsiste: em, sīc volō.

    Stand here, next to him. There, that’s how I want it.Ter. Ad. 170

  • tum in prātulō propter Platōnis statuam cōnsēdimus

    then we sat down on a little lawn beside the statue of PlatoCic. Brut. 24

  • ībat rēx obsitus aevō et comitem Aenēān juxtā nātumque tenēbat ingrediēns variōque viam sermōne levābat

    the king, weighed down with years, walked on, keeping Aeneas and his son beside him, and lightened the way with talkVerg. A. 8.307–309

  • mōre rēgum ut sellam juxtā pōneret

    (he asked) to set his chair beside him, as kings doSall. Jug. 65.2

  • cētera intēctī tōtōs diēs juxtā focum atque ignem agunt

    otherwise unclothed, they spend whole days by the hearth and the fireTac. Germ. 17.1

See also near, at, between, build.

SourcesLewis & Short: juxta · Lewis & Short: propter
